Division of Rehabilitation, Department of Clinical Practice and Support, Hiroshima University Hospital, Kasumi 1-2-3, Minami-ku, Hiroshima, 734-8551 Japan Abstract Introduction The differential diagnosis of plasmablastic lymphoma (PBL) form plasmablastic myeloma (PBM) is sometime very difficult. In such cases, the diagnosis of plasmablastic neoplasm (PBN) is acceptable. But clinicians face the question whether chemotherapies for PBL, PBM or othe rs are effective for PBN and the question increases the diagnosis dilemma. Although evidence on the differential diagnosis and treatment of those three entities is compiling, there is no scoping review of different diagnosis and treatment for PBL, PBM, and PBN to answer those questions. The aim of this study is to develop an a priori protocol to undertake a scoping review of the

steps.title: available evidence on the reproducibility of...
steps.instruction: available evidence on the reproducibility of differential diagnosis and the treatment of PBL, PBM, and PBN. Methods and analysis For the conducting the scoping review protocol, we will use an scoping review methodology established in the Joanna Briggs Institute manual. This methodology has a five -stage approach: (1) identify the research question; (2) identify relevant studies; (3) select studies; (4) chart the data and (5) collating, summarize and report the results. We also will use the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews to assess the results. Ethics and dissemination Since this is a review of the literature, ethics approval is not indicated. We will disseminate the findings from this study in publications in peer-reviewed journals.

steps.title: PBM, and PBN and the research questions are as followed
steps.instruction: PBM, and PBN and the research questions are as followed: 1. “What pathological characteristics of patients are diagnosed as PBL, PBM and PBN?” 2. “What regimens are used and what is the prognosis of PBL, PBM and PBN?” Stage 2: Identifying relevant studies We used the Population, Concept, and Context (PCC) framework by the JBI for scoping review(Peters et al., 2015) to define the inclusion criteria as follows: Participants All studies that include patients with PBL, PBM or PBN according to the WHO classification(Swerdlow SH, 2017) or author's definition will be included. No restrictions regarding age, ethnicity, any other characteristics will be made. Concept We will review the existing literature on diagnosis and treatments of PBL, PBM and PBN. Context We will not limit the context to cultural factors such as geographic location, specific racial or gender or particular settings such as acute care, primary health care or the community. A systematic search will perform using a three-step literature search. The first step will include an initial limited search of the MEDLINE. Then, we will carry out analyses of the text contained in the titles and abstracts and the index terms of retrieved papers. In second step to identify as many relevant studies as possible, the following databases will be searched: MEDLINE, CENTRAL, Embace, ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO-ICTRP. The search strategies for those databases were drafted by YK and HM and further refined through discussion (table 1). Third, we will check the reference lists of the included studies to search other resources. We will include any types of study design until April 2020 . Conference abstracts and systematic reviews will be excluded. Table 1. steps.title: In the study selection process, we...
steps.instruction: In the study selection process, we will adopt the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analysis (PRISMA) flow diagram (Moher et al., 2009). We will apply the inclusion and exclusion criteria described above for the selection of studies. The process will be carried out independently by two researchers (HM and HO). When there is any disagreement, we reach an agreement by discussion. Reasons for excluded studies will be reported. We will conduct the pilot testing using a random sample of 25 citations for title and abstracts screening. If level of agreement does not reach 75% (or greater), the eligibility criteria will be modified. Modifications will be reported in detail in the full scoping review report. Stage 4: Charting the data We will also use the data extraction summary form of patients’ characteristics (table 2) such as age, gender, performance status, Lugano stage, Ann Arbor stage, International Prognostic Index (IPI) score, tumor localization, status of HIV infection or immunodeficiency. We will count and calculate those data from case series or case reports. We will repot the percentage or data in cohort studies or others. We will group those data by PBL, PBM and PBN.

For each categorical or unknow data when reporting, a judgement will be made using one of three categories as follow: ● +: if the categorical data was described and positive ● -: if the categorical data was described and negative ● ?: if the report did not provide sufficient information When we report data derived from case series, we will give each patient a number, for example patient 1, patient 2 and patient 3. All results will be exported to Microsoft Excel 2016(Microsoft Corporation). Stage 5: Collating, summarizing, and reporting the results First, we will present the results of the search in the PRISMA flow chart. Second, we will organize the extracted data described above. The results of this scoping review will be presented as a map, in diagrammatic form, table and descriptive format. Differences between the protocol and the overview Changes in the methodology that need to be carried out throughout the study will be described in the results section. Ethics and dissemination This study will analyze only data of previously conducted studies, and will not involve any new studies performed by the authors. We will prepare the publication in accordance with PRISMA guideline and its adaptation for scoping reviews. We will publish our findings in peer -
reviewed journals. Patients and or public involvement Patients and or public were not involved in the development of this protocol. The study group developed this study protocol without patient involvement. Discussion We believe that this scoping review will constitute foundational knowledge and provide evidence on the reproducibility of the differential diagnosis and treatment of PBL, PBM and PBN. Currently, mos t reviews revolving around differential diagnosis and treatments are narrative reviews ( Castillo et al., 2015 , Harmon and Smith, 2016 , Lopez and Abrisqueta, 2018), which did not have the robust methodology. description: Background Plasmablastic lymphoma(PBL) is classified into a very aggressive lymphoma presenting immunoblasts or plasmablasts and having plasma cell phenotypes(Swerdlow SH, 2017). PBL is diagnosed at advanced stages, resulting in poor prognosis and a median overall survival 8 months(Han, 2017). Due to the rare disease, the standard chemotherapy has not been established. The differential diagnosis of PBL form plasmablastic myeloma (PBM) is sometime very difficult. PBL with plasmacytic differentiation has morphological and immunophenotypic features overlapping with those of PBM, especially extramedually PBM. The absence of serum monoclonal protein and lytic bone lesion, the high proliferation index or positive of In situ hybridization for EBV-encoded small RNA (EBER) make the diagnosis of PBM unlikely (Delecluse et al., 1997,Vega et al., 2005, Gravelle et al., 2018). But some cases presents both characteristics of PBL and PBM(Cencini et al., 2016, Dittus et al., 2018). Therefore those feature cannot make clear differential diagnosis of PBL from PBM and diagnosis is sometime arbitrary(Castillo et al., 2015). In such cases, descriptive diagnosis "plasmablastic neoplasm, consistent with PBL or anaplastic plasmacytoma" is possible to be accepted(Swerdlow SH, 2017). Clinicians face the question whether chemotherapies used for PBL, PBM, or others will be effective for PBN and the question increases the diagnostic dilemma. Currently most reviews are narrative reviews , especially of only PBL(Castillo et al., 2015, Harmon and Smith, 2016, Lopez and Abrisqueta, 2018), which are not suited to answer those dilemma and question. Therefore, the aim of this study is to conduct a scoping review to examine the available evidence on the reproducibility of differential diagnosis and the treatment of PBL, PBM, and PBN. Methods In preparing this protocol manuscript, the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews (PRISMA-ScR)(Tricco et al., 2018) statement was used. This proposed scoping review
